series_short_description: Growing up in Virginia Beach as autistic fraternal twins, Katie and Nathaniel ("Nate") Prairie build an unbreakable sibling sanctuary to weather school heartbreaks, family storms, and the Blizzard of '96.
series_description: Katie & Nathaniel follows the childhood and teenage years of autistic fraternal twins Katie and Nathaniel ("Nate") Prairie (born April 8, 1985) in Virginia Beach. From secret afternoon cartoon passwords, summer camp at Virginia Dominion University alongside Michael and Rachel Ragsdale, and holiday sofa-bed sanctuaries to the historic Blizzard of '96, middle-school Spirit Week, and their sixteen-year-old summer sanctuary watching Journey to the Sunlit Valley, Nate and Katie discover that while the outside world—and their mother's alcoholism—can be loud and unforgiving, twin brothers and sisters never leave each other behind.

parts.image_alt: At golden-hour sunset on the open wooden aft deck of the M/S Sunward Tropics cruise ship overlooking the Caribbean wake, sixteen-year-old fraternal twins Katie and Nathaniel Prairie sit side by side in ship-provided folding manual wheelchairs holding hands at a round deck table with their father David Prairie, sharing hot pizza and tall soda tumblers

parts.excerpt: Armed with the cruise ship's Deck 4 security tape, David files an immediate fault-based divorce and custody action in Virginia Beach—just as Nathaniel and Katie return to Northwood High School for their Junior year and share the daily lunch period they earned in summer school.
parts.image_alt: Inside the sunlit cafeteria of Northwood High School in Virginia Beach in September 2001, sixteen-year-old fraternal twins Katie and Nathaniel Prairie sit side by side at a quiet corner table holding hands during their shared Junior-year lunch period with their lunch bags and coding notebook open before them

parts.location: Virginia Beach, VA (Northwood High School, Bayside General Hospital ER, & Dr. Evelyn Carter's Consultation)
parts.excerpt: Forty-five minutes before Friday's 2:00 PM dismissal for their 3:00 PM doctor's appointment, Nathaniel and Katie's legs finally give out for good at Northwood High School—triggering an Emergency Room escalation after both twins collapse a second time, hit their heads on the floor, and immediately reach out to hold hands.

chapters.chap_title: Drunken New Year

parts.excerpt: When cousin Brittany defies the house ground rules on New Year's Eve 2002 by inviting friends and a twenty-one-year-old to buy gas-station alcohol, seventeen-year-old Nathaniel and Katie hide in a locked bedroom with a box of dry cereal—cementing why Nathaniel never had a twenty-first birthday drink.

parts.location: Virginia Beach, VA (Northwood High School & Rental House off Military Highway)
parts.excerpt: On the first morning back from winter break, a spiteful lie from one of Brittany's New Year's Eve partygoers turns Heather bitter against a blindsided Nathaniel—and Katie holds her heartbroken twin brother together when Heather abruptly ends the relationship.

parts.location: Norfolk, VA (Greenway Court, Apartment A6 — West Ghent)
parts.excerpt: Newly eighteen and graduated from Northwood High School, Katie and Nate settle into their first studio apartment together in Apartment A6 on Greenway Court—where Dad brings a rolling cart for their microwave and toaster, and they discover familiar faces from Delaney Street moving into Apartment A5 right across the hall.

parts.part_title: Part 2: Brenda in the Back Alley, Hiding in the Square Closet, & A Happy Year Together
parts.location: Norfolk, VA (Greenway Court, Apartment A6 & Downtown Norfolk)
parts.excerpt: When their estranged mother Brenda slips into the first-floor back alley behind the exterior iron stairs at Greenway Court looking for their window, eighteen-year-old Katie and Nate hide inside the dark square closet in their shared sleeping bag and fall fast asleep—discovering the deep-pressure closet sanctuary that anchors their happy year together in Apartment A6.

parts.excerpt: Celebrating the end of their freshman spring finals at the Community College of Hampton Roads in May 2004, nineteen-year-old Nate and Katie roll into Chapters & Co. at The Admiral Center—where a falling web-design paperback introduces Nate to twenty-year-old Tiffany Sloan.
parts.image_alt: Inside the computer books aisle of Chapters & Co. bookstore at The Admiral Center in Downtown Norfolk in May 2004, nineteen-year-old fraternal twins Nathaniel and Katie Prairie sit in their compact SwiftChair power wheelchairs holding cups of iced cocoa while twenty-year-old Tiffany Sloan hands Nathaniel a web-design book with a warm smile

parts.location: Norfolk, VA (Greenway Court, Apartment A6 — West Ghent)
parts.excerpt: When Tiffany Sloan visits Apartment A6 on Greenway Court the next afternoon with pizza and a floppy disk of her HTML files, she wins over both Nate and Katie with her kindness and respect for their twin bond.
parts.image_alt: Inside Apartment A6 on Greenway Court in May 2004, nineteen-year-old twins Nathaniel and Katie Prairie sit in their compact SwiftChair power wheelchairs beside their workstation desk with an open pizza box and cans of ginger ale on the rolling cart while Tiffany Sloan kneels warmly on the carpet between their wheelchairs holding a floppy disk

parts.location: Norfolk, VA (Greenway Court, Apartment A6 — West Ghent)
parts.excerpt: After three idyllic summer months of dating Nate, Tiffany Sloan gently convinces Nate and Katie that she and Nate should move into a ground-floor one-bedroom apartment at Sea Breeze West in West Ocean View—promising that Katie is only one Route 1 bus ride away and that the twins will still have Brother-and-Sister Weekends together.

chapters.chap_title: Ocean View Station, Dirty Old Tonomy Hill, & Five Buses from Williamsburg

parts.part_title: Part 1: Ocean View Station, The Green Sofa Confrontation, & Speak Now or Forever Hold Your Peace
parts.location: Norfolk, VA (Ocean View Station & Sea Breeze West Apartment 3 on West Ocean View Avenue)
parts.excerpt: When nineteen-year-old Katie rides the CVTA Route 1 bus to Ocean View Station for a brother-and-sister weekend with Nate at Sea Breeze West, Tiffany Sloan's jealous outburst prompts Katie to swear her Speak Now or Forever Hold Your Peace vow.
parts.image_alt: Inside the Sea Breeze West living room on West Ocean View Avenue, nineteen-year-old twins Katie in her royal-blue V-neck sweater and Nate in his brick-red polo sit side by side on the bright green three-cushion sofa beneath the white window blinds with their compact SwiftChair power wheelchairs parked beside the oval coffee table while Tiffany Sloan glares through her black-rimmed glasses in her mint-green graphic shirt by the corner CRT television

parts.part_title: Part 2: Riding Route 1 Back to West Ghent, Meeting Brandon Mercer at The Admiral Center, & Taking Things Slow
parts.location: Norfolk, VA (Greenway Court, Apartment A6 & The Admiral Center in Ghent)
parts.excerpt: Riding the Route 1 bus down from Ocean View on Sunday afternoon to apologize to Katie for their ruined Brother-and-Sister Weekend, Nate finds his twin sister at The Admiral Center talking with twenty-two-year-old Williamsburg visitor Brandon Mercer—who presents himself as a total gentleman, assumes last night wasn't Nate's fault, and respects Katie's wish to get to know him slowly.

parts.part_title: Part 3: Patience at Katie's Pace, Winning Over Nate and Dad, & Katie's Move to Williamsburg
parts.location: Norfolk, VA (Greenway Court, Apartment A6 — West Ghent)
parts.excerpt: After two months of patiently visiting Norfolk every weekend at Katie's pace and winning the trust of Katie, Nate, and their father David, Brandon Mercer gently convinces a lonely Katie to move out of Apartment A6 into his ground-floor apartment on Virginia Avenue in Williamsburg right before the holidays.

parts.part_title: Part 4: The Worst Christmas Ever: Eighteen Stops to Dirty Old Tonomy Hill, Four Days with Cousin Chelsea, & The West Main Road Shortcut Home
parts.location: Newport, RI (Tonomy Hill Apartments) & Interstate 95 / Interstate 64 South
parts.excerpt: After an eighteen-stop northbound Pathfinder and OSTA bus haul to Newport's World War II-era Tonomy Hill public housing apartments for Cousin Chelsea's first Christmas without Aunt Liz, nineteen-year-old Nathaniel endures four days of Tiffany Sloan's cruel jealousy before riding OSTA Route 60 and Pathfinder back to Virginia.

parts.part_title: Part 5: Five Buses from Williamsburg — The Ninety-Second Window, Crown Burger, & The Last Route 61 Across the Water

parts.excerpt: When Brandon Mercer marches twenty-year-old Katie from 224 Virginia Avenue to the Williamsburg Transportation Center to buy one-way rail and tunnel-bus tickets to Windsor, Canada, she seizes a ninety-second window while he is at the ticket counter to roll aboard the 4:00 PM CTTA Grey Line bus—beginning a grueling five-bus escape through the November rain to reach her twin brother Nate in West Ocean View.
parts.image_alt: Inside the living room of Sea Breeze West Apartment 3 on the rainy Saturday night of November 12, 2005 after Katie's five-bus escape from Williamsburg, twenty-year-old Katie sits wrapped in a dry towel and Nate's navy-blue sleeping bag on the bright green sofa while her twin brother Nate holds both of her hands from his compact SwiftChair power wheelchair

chapters.chap_title: The End of Hell & Reclaiming Apartment 3

parts.part_title: Part 1: A Sister's Worst Nightmare, Tiffany Forces a Choice, & Scrubbing Out the Filth
parts.location: Norfolk, VA (Sea Breeze West Apartment 3 & Crown Burger on West Ocean View Avenue)
parts.excerpt: After escaping Williamsburg on five consecutive buses in the pouring rain to reach Nate's filthy Sea Breeze West apartment in West Ocean View, twenty-year-old Katie helps Nate break free from Tiffany Sloan, scrub their sanctuary clean, and make their lifelong fifty-fifty pact.

Inside the living room of Sea Breeze West Apartment 3 in front of the bright green three-cushion sofa and the front windows with white horizontal mini-blinds at night: twenty-year-old Katie in her mustard-yellow ringer t-shirt and blue jeans sits in her compact black SwiftChair power wheelchair with tears rolling down her cheeks as she holds twenty-year-old Nate's hand across their wheelchairs and promises her brother that they will never separate ever again

parts.part_title: Part 3: The Goyeau Street Tunnel Bus, The Federal Courthouse on Granby Street, & Protected Non-Traveling Complainant
parts.location: Norfolk, VA (Walter E. Hoffman United States Courthouse — 600 Granby Street)
parts.excerpt: On Wednesday afternoon, November 16, 2005, Dad accompanies Katie and Nate to the Walter E. Hoffman United States Courthouse in Downtown Norfolk—where Special Agent Morales pulls up the Sunday afternoon CBSA and U.S. CBP border refusal file from the Goyeau Street tunnel plaza in Windsor and East Jefferson Avenue in Detroit, proving Brandon Mercer handed federal prosecutors the entire case against himself.

parts.excerpt: Ten days after reclaiming Apartment 3, Nate and Katie share Thanksgiving dinner with their father David at his house in Virginia Beach, and on Black Friday weekend David builds the half-pantry, half-coat hallway closet—discovering the sleeping bag and two pillows where his autistic twins have been sleeping every night instead of Tiffany's bed.

parts.part_title: Part 5: The Seattle Transit Blog Inspiration & Quietly Launching Ideas for Coastal Virginia Transit
parts.location: Norfolk, VA (Sea Breeze West Apartment 3 — 233 West Ocean View Avenue)
parts.excerpt: Inspired by the Seattle Transit Blog covering TAPS in the Puget Sound, Nate and Katie sit side by side at their freshly formatted Quantum OS XN Pro desktop in Apartment 3, hand-code a custom HTML template on BlogSphere, and quietly launch Ideas for Coastal Virginia Transit.

chapters.chap_title: Do Better: The Four-Bus Loop, Kempsville City Council, & The Path to the 85th House District

parts.part_title: Part 1: Does the Bus Run? Calling Out CVTA's Complacency & The 2008 Regional Mayoral Challenge
parts.location: Norfolk & Virginia Beach, VA (CVTA Headquarters on 18th Street & Kempsville Home Office)
parts.excerpt: As Ideas for Coastal Virginia Transit gains regional attention and confronts CVTA's 'good enough' complacency, Nate and Katie issue an open 2008 transit challenge to mayoral candidates across Virginia Beach, Chesapeake, Portsmouth, and Hampton—receiving a single acceptance from a Virginia Beach mayoral candidate.

parts.part_title: Part 2: The Four-Bus Mayoral Loop, Silenced at Eighteenth Street, & Choosing to Run for the Kempsville Seat
parts.location: Virginia Beach & Norfolk, VA (CCHR Bus Loop, CVTA Routes 29/20/15/12, & 509 E. 18th Street)
parts.excerpt: Riding a four-bus circuit (#29 -> #20 -> #15 -> #12) with Virginia Beach mayoral candidate Scott Tanner, Nate and Katie expose the expired two-hour transfer penalty and the 5:48 PM evening bus curfew—and after CVTA executives cut off Nate's microphone and blackball him from TRAC while Councilman Harold Dietz kills evening bus service, Katie decides to run for the Kempsville City Council seat.

parts.part_title: Part 3: The Empty Podium on WHRC TV-15, The 8:24 PM Three-Bus Sprint Home, & The Front-Page Metro Headline
parts.location: Norfolk & Virginia Beach, VA (WHRC TV-15 Studios on Hampton Boulevard, CVTA Routes 2/20/15, & Lord Nelson Drive)
parts.excerpt: When incumbent Councilman Harold Dietz fails to RSVP for the live WHRC TV-15 debate, twenty-five-year-old Katie commands the studio broadcast beside his brightly lit empty mahogany podium—and then stunned Tidewater Pilot reporter Greg Mercer sprints across six lanes of Hampton Boulevard with Katie and Nate as they race to catch the 8:24 PM Route 2 bus home.

parts.part_title: Part 4: The WTGA 790 AM Disability Attack, The 94.1% Landslide, & The Eighteenth Street Reckoning
parts.location: Virginia Beach & Norfolk, VA (Lord Nelson Drive in Kempsville, Virginia Beach Municipal Center Building 1, & 509 E. 18th Street)
parts.excerpt: Five days before the election, a desperate Councilman Harold Dietz calls into conservative talk radio WTGA 790 AM to attack Katie's wheelchair and question the taxpayer cost of a City Hall dais ramp—triggering a nuclear backlash across Hampton Roads, an unprecedented 94.1% to 5.9% Election Night landslide, and a historic reckoning for CVTA's executive suite.

parts.part_title: Part 5: Stopped at the Third-Floor Gallery by Capitol Police, Seated on the House Floor Near Delegate Ronald Villa, & The Spark to Run
parts.location: Richmond, VA (Virginia State Capitol Third-Floor Gallery Corridor & House of Delegates Floor)
parts.excerpt: Visiting Richmond in February 2012 during her second year on the Virginia Beach City Council to testify for state transit funding, twenty-six-year-old Katie and Nate head upstairs to the third-floor public viewing gallery—only to be stopped by Capitol Police over emergency-evacuation safety concerns and granted the rare honor by House Leadership of sitting right on the Floor of the Virginia House of Delegates near former Virginia Beach City Councilman and State Delegate Ronald Villa.

parts.part_title: Part 6: Telling Dad at Our Kempsville Kitchen Table, The 125-Signature Ballot Petition at CCHR, & Winning the Eighty-Fifth House District
parts.location: Virginia Beach, VA (Lord Nelson Drive in Kempsville, CCHR Bus Loop, & Virginia Beach Municipal Center)
parts.excerpt: Sitting down with their father David at their Kempsville kitchen table, Katie and Nate brainstorm every legal and grassroots step of a 2013 Virginia House of Delegates campaign—from filing her candidate qualification paperwork and collecting 400 voter signatures at CCHR to defeating Delegate Richard Tatum in the 85th District and wrapping up her service on the Virginia Beach City Council.

chapters.chap_title: Freshman Session on West Broad Street & Riding JRTC Route 6 to the Capitol

parts.part_title: Part 1: The West Broad Street Loft, Unpacking Our Shared Queen Bed, & Weekend Reconnaissance on JRTC Route 6
parts.location: Richmond, VA (Broad & Boulevard Lofts on West Broad Street & Oak Lawn)
parts.excerpt: Five days before the 2014 Virginia General Assembly convenes for Freshman Delegate Katie Prairie's first legislative session, Nate, Katie, and their dad unpack their furnished one-bedroom apartment on West Broad Street—spending the weekend buying regular 30-day JRTC bus passes and mapping out Route 6 between Oak Lawn and Capitol Square.

parts.part_title: Part 2: Gold License Plates vs. JRTC Route 6, Turning Down the Parking Deck Pass, & The 60-Inch ADA Restroom Showdown
parts.location: Richmond, VA (Ninth & Broad Street, General Assembly Building, & Virginia State Capitol)
parts.excerpt: Arriving for New Member Orientation on Monday morning, Freshman Delegate Katie Prairie and Nate shock veteran lawmakers and lobbyists by rolling down the front ramp of a JRTC Route 6 city bus at Ninth and Broad—before turning down her legislative parking pass and forcing Capitol Facilities to fix the non-compliant restroom stalls before Opening Day.

chapters.chap_title: House Bill 663

parts.part_title: Part 1: Line 18, Seated by Delegate Ronald Villa on the Floor, & A Question Across the Chamber
parts.location: Richmond, VA (Capitol Tunnel & Virginia State Capitol House of Delegates Floor)
parts.excerpt: Before the Thursday noon session of the Virginia House of Delegates, Nate and Delegate Katie Prairie review the printed text of House Bill 663 as they roll through the Capitol tunnel—before Katie takes her accessible desk on the minority aisle and Nate rolls to his designated ADA floor bay beside Virginia Beach Delegate Ronald Villa to record her floor question.

parts.part_title: Part 2: Thursday Evening at Six, Friday on Capitol Square, & Sunday Morning on Meet the Nation
parts.location: Richmond, VA (Winter-Session Apartment, Capitol Square, & GBS Richmond Studio)
parts.excerpt: Returning to their Richmond apartment on Thursday evening, Nate and Katie turn on the television to find Richmond and Norfolk local news stations carrying her House Floor speech—leading to live local interviews on Friday and a Sunday morning appearance on Meet the Nation.

chapters.chap_title: Across the Rotunda: Why Run for State Senate, The 7th District Race, & Madam Chair

parts.part_title: Part 1: Watching Senator Ward Kill Our Bills Across the Rotunda, Brainstorming the 7th Senate District with Dad, & The 250-Signature Rule
parts.location: Richmond & Virginia Beach, VA (Senate Room A, Capitol Rotunda, & 741 Lord Nelson Drive in Kempsville)
parts.excerpt: After watching twenty-year incumbent State Senator Franklin Ward of Virginia Beach casually gavel her hard-won House transit and developmental-disability waiver bills to death in a Senate committee, thirty-two-year-old Delegate Katie Prairie sits down with Nate and their dad David to map out her 2019 campaign for the 7th Senate District.

parts.part_title: Part 2: Flipping the Seventh Senate District, Custom-Milling the Mahogany Senate Ramp, & Swearing In as Madam Chair
parts.location: Virginia Beach & Richmond, VA (Kempsville Headquarters & The Senate of Virginia Chamber at the State Capitol)
parts.excerpt: On November 5, 2019, thirty-four-year-old Katie Prairie wins the 7th Senate District to help flip the Senate of Virginia into a new majority—working with the Clerk of the Senate to install a permanent custom-milled mahogany wheelchair ramp on the Senate Floor before swearing her oath on the Constitution of Virginia as Chair of Rehabilitation and Social Services.

chapters.chap_title: Election Night, The Decision Desk Call, & The Referendum Mandate

parts.part_title: Part 1: Polls Close at Seven, The 8:42 PM Decision Desk Call, & Victory in Virginia Beach
parts.location: Virginia Beach, VA (Kempsville & The Virginia Beach Convention Ballroom)
parts.excerpt: On Election Night in Virginia Beach, Nate tracks precinct returns on their custom PHP dashboard until the GNN, GBS, and Beacon News Decision Desks project forty-one-year-old State Senator Katie Prairie as the newest United States Senator from Virginia.
parts.image_alt: Forty-one-year-old U.S. Senator-Elect Katie Prairie and her fraternal twin brother Nate hold hands across their compact SwiftChair power wheelchairs on a ballroom stage in Virginia Beach with their proud father David standing on his own two feet beside them beneath falling confetti and the GNN Decision Desk projection screen

parts.excerpt: When the Senate website vendor tries to brush Senator-Elect Katie Prairie off with a ZIP file of minified code, Katie demands the raw unminified repository with the bewildered build team on speakerphone—and both twins erupt in fury over the barely commented, WCAG-failing source code.

parts.location: Richmond, VA (The Virginia State Capitol & The Office of the Clerk of the Senate of Virginia)
parts.excerpt: Because Article IV, Section 4 of the Constitution of Virginia forbids holding both a state legislative seat and federal office, State Senator Katie Prairie travels to the Virginia State Capitol in Richmond with Nate to formally hand-deliver her resignation to the Clerk of the Senate.
parts.image_alt: Inside the historic neoclassical Clerk's Office of the Senate of Virginia at the State Capitol in Richmond, forty-one-year-old State Senator and U.S. Senator-Elect Katie Prairie sits in her compact SwiftChair power wheelchair alongside her twin brother Nate in his matching powerchair and formally hands her gold-sealed parchment resignation letter across the mahogany counter to the Clerk of the Senate

chapters.chap_title: First Train from Norfolk & Swearing In on the Constitution

parts.location: Norfolk & Alexandria, VA (Norfolk Station NFK, ARTS Northeast Regional, & Alexandria Union Station ALX)
parts.excerpt: On the morning of her U.S. Senate swearing-in, forty-one-year-old Senator-Elect Katie Prairie, her twin brother Nate, and their dad David ride the 5:00 AM ARTS Business Class train from Norfolk for the free Café Car drinks—and shock commuters by detraining on the mobile lift at Alexandria instead of Washington Union Station.

parts.part_title: Part 3: The First Invite to Cocktails, A Known Side Effect of Death, & Home to Sunset Drive
parts.location: Washington, D.C. & Alexandria, VA (The Mansfield Room at the U.S. Capitol, Capital Transit Yellow Line, & The Brick House on Sunset Drive)
parts.excerpt: Invited to her first Senate leadership cocktail reception, Senator Katie Prairie establishes that she, Nate, and their dad take a daily medication where mixing with alcohol or tobacco has a known side effect of death—before riding the Yellow Line back to their two-story brick house on Sunset Drive.

chapters.chap_title: The Norfolk Carrier Leak, Madison & Lincoln, & Three Convictions in the Senate

parts.part_title: Part 1: The South Lawn Tirade, The Norfolk Carrier Leak, & Why the Order of the Trials Matters
parts.location: Washington, D.C. (Room 511 of the Dirksen Senate Office Building & The Senate Commerce Committee)
parts.excerpt: When President Garrett Thorne rails on the South Lawn against 'Broken Katie Prairie' and her twin brother Nate for stalling his nominees and exposing the $400 million Naval Station Norfolk carrier-schedule leak by Defense Secretary Bret Halverson and Vice President Julian Vance, Katie and Speaker Clara Morales set an airtight constitutional trap.

parts.part_title: Part 2: The Words of Mason, Madison, and Lincoln, Three Guilty Votes in Forty-Eight Hours, & Swearing In President Clara Morales
parts.location: Washington, D.C. (The United States Senate Chamber & The Mansfield Room at the U.S. Capitol)
parts.excerpt: Sitting at her custom-height mahogany floor desk in the United States Senate while Nate and Dad watch from the Senate Family Gallery, Senator Katie Prairie quotes George Mason, James Madison, and Abraham Lincoln—casting her Guilty votes to convict, remove, and permanently disqualify Defense Secretary Bret Halverson, Vice President Julian Vance, and President Garrett Thorne, elevating Speaker Clara Morales to the Presidency.
